case_name: Badri and Others v State of Uttar Pradesh
respondent:
State of Uttar Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

29 July 1975
Cr.A. No. 39 of 1972.
The Judgment was delivered by: BHAGWATI, J.
1.  for the The appellants and one Tulsi Das were charged for offences u/ss. 302 and 201, read with S. 149 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. the appellants were also charged for offence u/s. 148 and Tulsi Das for offences u/s. 147. The Sections Judge, Hamirpur acquitted the appellants and Tulsi Das of all the offences charged against them. The State preferred and appeal against the order of acquittal were concerned, and, setting aside the order of acquittal, convicted the appellants of offences u/s. 302 read with S. 149 as well as S. 148 and sentenced each of them to suffer life imprisonment for the offence under Section on 302 read with S. 149 and two years' rigorous imprisonment for the offence u/s. 148 with a direction that both sentences should run concurrently. The acquittal of the appellants for offence u/s. 201 read with S. 149 was confir
facts: The incident giving rise to the prosecution in the present case took place in village Aunts within the jurisdiction of police station Rath in Hamirpur district.

There were at the material time two factions in this village, one consisting of followers of the previous pradhan Bindaban and the other consisting of the followers of Ram Sevak who was pradhan then in the office.
The appellants belonged to the faction of Bindaban, while the deceased Chet Ram, who was also known as Karia, companions owed allegiance to the faction of Ram Sevak.

An incident took place on March 26, 1967 between appellants Nos. 1 and 2 and Tulsi Das on the one hand and one Maddu on the other in which the deceased Chet Ram and one Das assisted Maddu by taking him to the police station and lodging a report against appellants Nos. 1 and 2 and Tulsi Das.
This incident, according to the prosecution, roused the ire of the appellants and Tulsi Das which culminated in the attack on the deceased Chet Ram on the next day, that is, March 27, 1967.
issues: Whether the evidence on record establishes the guilt of the appellants beyond doubt
Whether the learned Sessions Judge erred in acquitting the appellants
petitioner_arguments: The theory of dragging was not believable and gave four reasons for taking this view.

It was likely that when Ram Dayal lodged the report at police station Rath, he did not know who were the real assailants of the deceased Chet Ram, but implicated the appellants only because the latter belonged to the faction of Bindaban.
respondent_arguments: The evidence on record did establish the guilt of the appellants beyond doubt
The learned Sessions Judge had erred in acquitting the appellants
court_reasoning: There was nothing inherently improbable in the conduct of the appellant in removing the dead body of the deceased Chet Ram from the courtyard of Laxmi by dragging it.
The High Court pointed out that the time and place of the incident were established beyond question and they were not challenged on behalf of the appellants.
holding: The State preferred an appeal against the order of acquittal to the High Court. The High Court closely scrutinised the evidence and on the appreciation of the evidence came to the conclusion that the learned Sessions Judge had erred in acquitting the appellants.
The High Court then proceeded to discuss the reasoning and demonstrated how in its opinion the reasoning was fallacious.
